Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

Job Description

Visa is seeking a proactive and strategic finance leader to join the Acceptance Solutions Finance team. As a senior finance leader supporting one of Visa's fastest-growing businesses, the Senior Director will partner closely with executives and cross-functional teams to provide the insights, analytics, and strategic guidance needed to drive sound business decisions.

The ideal candidate brings experience in strategic finance, consulting, investment banking, or a related field. They should be adept at solving complex problems, navigating ambiguity, and translating complex data into actionable insights that influence leadership decisions. Strong financial modeling, business partnership, strategic planning, resource allocation, and investment evaluation experience is preferred.

Finance Leadership & Business Partnership
- Serve as the finance leader supporting Acceptance Solutions businesses.
- Partner closely with Product, Technology, Commercial, Operations, and regional leadership teams to drive growth, profitability, and strategic decision-making.
- Build strong relationships and influence outcomes across a complex, matrixed organization.

Business Performance & Financial Insights
- Deliver actionable insights on revenue growth, payment volume, margins, transaction economics, pricing, and operating leverage.
- Partner with business leaders to evaluate performance drivers, assess risks and opportunities, and identify actions to improve results.
- Establish a clear connection between operational metrics and financial outcomes to improve visibility and decision-making across the organization.

Data, Analytics & Finance Transformation
- Partner around efforts to build scalable data foundations, dashboards, reporting, and analytics that connect operational performance to financial results.
- Drive simplification, automation, and AI-enabled improvements across finance processes and decision-support capabilities.
- Translate complex and often unstructured data into clear insights, actionable recommendations, and executive-level narratives.
- Drive operational excellence across key end-to-end business processes, partnering with Sales, Sales Operations, Pricing, Billing, Collections, and Finance teams to improve efficiency, scalability, controls, and business outcomes.

Leadership & Team Development
- Foster a culture of accountability, business partnership, analytical rigor, and continuous improvement.
- Coach and develop future finance leaders while driving strong execution and organizational impact.

This role is a People Manager Hybrid role to be located in our San Francisco office location. Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

- 12 or more years of work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 10 years of work experience with an Advanced degree (e.g. Masters/MBA /JD/MD), or a minimum of 5 years of work
- Strategic finance, consulting, investment banking background.
- Exceptional problem-solving and strategic thinking skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, synthesize complex information, and provide clear recommendations that influence leadership decision-making.
- Strong financial modeling, analytical, and business partnership capabilities, including experience evaluating investments, growth opportunities, resource allocation decisions, and business performance.
- Experience building data-driven reporting, analytics, and decision-support capabilities.
- Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive results across a highly matrixed organization.
- Strong executive communication and presentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications:
- 15 or more years of experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or 12 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, or MD), PhD with 9+ years of experience

rows.description:
Description:

Zafran is looking for an experienced Project Manager, Customer Success to join our expanding team. As our Customer Success team scales, we need someone to help it run smarter and deliver for our most important customers. Reporting to the Manager of Customer Success Strategy, the Project Manager will split their time between two areas. About half of the role is managing strategic customer projects, partnering with our TAMs to keep high-visibility deployments and enterprise initiatives on track. The other half is driving projects that improve how Customer Success works: streamlining processes, automating manual work, and rolling out new CS initiatives across the organization.



About Zafran:



Our Mission: To stop the exploitation of vulnerabilities, everywhere.



What makes us different: In a world where AI-enabled attackers weaponize vulnerabilities within minutes, the old scan-and-patch-everything model no longer holds. Zafran's Exposure Graph continuously maps every vulnerability across your hybrid environment, chains exploitability through real attack paths and proves 90% of "critical" vulnerabilities can't actually reach you. It then neutralizes the real 10% using your compensating controls and safely remediates only where it matters.



Who’s behind us: Zafran is backed by Menlo Ventures, Sequoia Capital, Cyberstarts, and a deep belief that cybersecurity should move as fast as attackers do. We’re one of the fastest-growing companies in the industry, scaling to meet demand from the world’s most advanced, security-obsessed organizations.



We’re serious about our mission- so expect work that matters, teammates who challenge and inspire you, and plenty of fun along the way!



What you will do:

 - Manage strategic customer projects, such as high-visibility deployments, large enterprise rollouts, and executive engagements, partnering with Solution Architects and TAMs to drive plans, timelines, and stakeholders from kickoff through delivery.

 - Lead projects that strengthen how the Customer Success team operates, from identifying gaps in current workflows to designing and implementing better ones.

 - Drive the rollout of new Customer Success initiatives, including planning, stakeholder alignment, enablement, and tracking adoption after launch.

 - Identify opportunities to automate manual or repetitive work across the customer lifecycle, and partner with GTM Ops, Engineering, and system owners to build and implement those automations.

 - Work across the organization (Sales, Product, Engineering, Support, Marketing, and Finance) to streamline cross-functional handoffs and make sure Customer Success has what it needs to deliver for customers.

 - Build and maintain playbooks, templates, and documentation that help the Solution Architect, Support and TAM teams work consistently and scale effectively.

 - Manage project plans, timelines, and dependencies for multiple internal initiatives at once, keeping stakeholders informed with clear status updates and reporting.

 - Measure the impact of process changes and new programs, and use that data to recommend further improvements.

 - Act as a trusted partner to Customer Success leadership, helping prioritize the initiatives that will have the biggest impact on the team and on customers.

Requirements:

 - 5+ years of project or program management experience, ideally in a B2B SaaS or customer-facing environment.

 - Experience supporting Customer Success, Professional Services, or Technical Account Management teams.

 - A proven ability to manage several projects at once without losing sight of details or deadlines.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills, with comfort presenting to both internal teams and customers.

 - Fluency with project management and collaboration tools (such as Jira, Asana, Monday.com http://Monday.com, Notion, or Slack) and a CRM like Salesforce; familiarity with Zendesk is a plus.

 - Enough technical curiosity to understand the product and hold your own in conversations with engineers and technical customers; familiarity with cybersecurity is a strong plus.

 - A process-minded approach: you notice what’s being done manually or inconsistently and build a better way.

 - Calm, organized, and proactive under pressure, with good judgment about when to escalate.

 - A customer-first mindset and a genuine interest in helping customers succeed.

 - PMP or similar certification is a plus but not required.



At Zafran, people matter! We provide a robust benefits program that includes flexible PTO, health insurance plans (medical, dental, vision), a monthly stipend for phone and internet, 401k, flexible spending account, and a home office stipend when joining!



We also provide access to frontier AI models, including Claude, so every employee can work smarter, move faster, and build an AI-first career from day one.



At Zafran, we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the best teams are built by people who think differently, come from all kinds of backgrounds, and aren’t afraid to challenge the status quo. We welcome everyone across race, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, national origin, and veteran status, because what matters most is what you bring to the table.



If you’re curious, fun, and someone who gets things done, we’d love to meet you

The ideal candidate will bring deep, hands-on experience across retail supply chain functions including Space Planning, Assortment Planning, Planning & Allocation, Logistics & Transportation, Vendor Chargebacks, and Supply Chain Operations. - Proven experience leading large global teams in shared services or global operations environments.

rows.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

The Procurement Manager, Direct role is responsible for total accountability of strategy and execution for fulfillment of orders relating to Subcontract Supply Chain (externally manufactured). This role sits at the intersection of sourcing and requisition, contract management, and supplier performance: acting as the connective tissue between our customers, internal teams, and supply base. You will be accountable owner of full lifecycle from RFQ through PO delivery, ensuring we hit cost, quality, and schedule targets while building the supplier relationships that sustain long-term program success. This role is a critical function in developing a world class procurement service prioritizing quality, cost, and speed.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Own the supplier selection and sourcing strategy for demand relating to externally manufactured requirements from end-customers and internal factory ops needs

 - Operate as the primary point of direction to the supporting functions of the org across buyers, coordinators, supplier quality, and internal factory ops and customer facing groups.

 - Managing operational KPIs and taking proper action to improve performance as it relates to transactional SLAs, quality, delivery, and cost

 - Develop long term strategies that support various customer and organizational objective, such as: cost down initiatives, quality improvements, supply base growth and strategy, capacity analysis and rate ramp readiness

 - Operate as escalation path for negotiation, commercial resolution, and in-process order fulfillment

 - Ensure compliance with all company and customer policies, requirements, procedures and government regulations while acting with integrity and prioritizing the needs of company and programs

 - Present value propositions, open risks, and health of supply base and order book to leadership

 - Manage the creation and evolution of governing standard operating procedures and working closely with the internal product and software team on developing adequate tool set to consistently improve operations

 - Work with suppliers and relevant internal functions on technical review of specifications, providing design for manufacturability and supply chain feedback where and when applicable

 - Work with internal quoting teams on make versus buy analysis and decision making as it relates to manufacturing parts through internal core factory or externally through managed supply base

 - Work closely with open order management group to ensure blockers and risks are addressed with priority and proactively actioning to prevent future issues

 - Understand business needs at a high level to proactively take action and direct team to operate in a way that sets the company up for success at scale

 - Periodically visit suppliers on-site to ensure alignment on growth plans, strategy, performance feedback and guidance, and resolution of any blockers or points of friction

 

What We’re Looking For

 - Bachelor's or advanced degree with 5+ years of experience working in one or more of the following:
   
   - Engineering (mechanical, aerospace, chemical, materials)
   
   - Purchasing/Procurement (CNC machining, forgings, metallic raw materials, sheet metal, production tooling)
   
   - Contract Negotiation
   
   - Supply Chain Management
   
   - Material / Demand Planning

 - Experience in identifying and executing an optimized machining supply chain, or other complex supply chain systems in advanced manufacturing sub-commodities

 

What Will Set You Apart

 - Demonstrated success in managing large value contracts and supply base while balancing high-frequency of change and effectively balancing trade-offs between quality, cost, and schedule

 - Ability to easily navigate technical engineering specifications (drawings, models, etc) with a fundamental understanding of how components should optimally be manufactured or built

 - Ability to learn program context quickly and prioritize items effectively so that goals are properly met

 - Exceptional communication skills and ability to successfully manage cross-functional teams across various factory operations functions

 

Compensation

For this role, the target salary range is $130,000 - $170,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

rows.description:
UnitedHealth Group is a health care and well-being company that's dedicated to improving the health outcomes of millions around the world. We are comprised of two distinct and complementary businesses, UnitedHealthcare and Optum, working to build a better health system for all. Here, your contributions matter as they will help transform health care for years to come. Make an impact with a team that shares your passion for helping others. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

The Director, Procurement Effectiveness - Optum Health will serve as a strategic customer success and governance leader for Enterprise Procurement supporting major Optum Health business partners, clinical stakeholders, and complex care delivery organizations. The role is responsible for (i) improving customer experience, (ii) strengthening stakeholder relationships, (iii) increasing visibility into Procurement work intake, and (iv) ensuring sourcing and supplier-related requests are progressing effectively across complex operating environments.

This position will act as a primary relationship and escalation partner for large or complex customer groups, helping translate business needs into actionable Procurement engagement, governance, reporting, and process-improvement priorities.

Strategic Purpose of the Role
This role exists to create a more consistent, proactive, and customer-centered Procurement experience across Optum Health by:
- Serving as a single strategic point of coordination for complex Procurement customer activity
- Improving visibility into procurement requests, supplier verification requests, governance workstreams, and customer escalations
- Strengthening relationships with clinical, operational, integration, and regional business leaders
- Identifying process gaps, cycle-time issues, handoff breakdowns, and customer pain points
- Driving continuous improvement in Procurement service delivery and customer satisfaction

Primary Responsibilities:
- Customer Success and Relationship Management - Serve as a Procurement customer success lead for large, complex, or high-priority Optum Health customer groups, including major CDOs and regional business partners and Acquired Entities
- Build and maintain trusted relationships with clinical governance/operations, care delivery operations, integration teams, category management, enterprise procurement, and executive stakeholders
- Act as the primary Procurement relationship partner for assigned customer segments, ensuring business needs are understood, translated, prioritized, and connected to the appropriate Procurement resources
- Facilitate proactive customer engagement to identify emerging service issues, recurring pain points, and opportunities to improve the Procurement experience
- Support leadership escalations by clarifying root cause, business impact, ownership, next steps, and resolution path

- Governance and Operating Rhythm Leadership - Lead or support Procurement governance routines across Optum Health, including executive-level updates, workstream reviews, regional report-outs and engagement, and customer-specific operating reviews
- Prepare clear, business-oriented reporting that summarizes request status, bottlenecks, risks, aging items, escalation themes, and recommended interventions
- Partner with Procurement leadership to ensure governance discussions are focused on business outcomes, service performance, customer experience, and decision-making needs
- Create transparency across multiple workstreams by connecting customer feedback, operational metrics, category activity, and sourcing progress
- Ensure major customer forums result in clear ownership, documented actions, and visible follow-through

- Procurement Service Experience and Process Effectiveness - Own the assessment of Procurement service effectiveness for assigned Optum Health customer groups
- Analyze process performance by customer/CDO, category team, category manager, workstream, and request type
- Identify recurring breakdowns in material request intake, supplier validation, handoffs, comments, approvals, and cycle-time performance
- Develop recommendations to improve turnaround time, customer communication, request quality, intake discipline, supplier transition support, and stakeholder satisfaction
- Partner with operational teams to implement improvement actions while maintaining clear distinction between strategic process ownership and tactical execution

- Analytics, Reporting, and Business Insights - Develop and interpret customer-facing metrics related to request volume, cycle time, aging, handoffs, bottlenecks, ownership, and customer experience
- Use data to identify where Procurement processes are working well and where customer experience is breaking down
- Translate operational data into executive-ready insights and actionable recommendations
- Partner with category, operations, and governance teams to create reporting that supports prioritization, accountability, and service improvement
- Present findings to Procurement and Optum Health leaders in a concise, financially and operationally relevant manner

- Escalation Management and Issue Resolution - Serve as a senior point of coordination for complex customer escalations requiring Procurement leadership attention
- Triage escalations by business impact, risk, urgency, stakeholder sensitivity, and required decision authority
- Coordinate with category leaders, sourcing teams, operations teams, legal, compliance, clinical stakeholders, and integration partners to move escalated issues toward resolution
- Ensure escalations are documented with clear ownership, decision points, dependencies, and customer communication expectations
- Identify patterns in escalations and recommend systemic changes to reduce repeat issues

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.
Required Qualifications:
- 7+ years of experience in procurement, sourcing, supply chain, customer success, operations, governance, process improvement, or related business functions
- Experience using data, reporting, and business insights to identify process gaps, cycle-time issues, service performance trends, and improvement opportunities
- Demonstrated experience managing complex stakeholder relationships across clinical, operational, procurement, legal, compliance, finance, and executive audiences
- Proven ability to lead governance routines, operating reviews, escalation processes, or cross-functional workstreams in a matrixed organization
- Demonstrated solid communication skills with the ability to translate complex operational issues into clear, executive-ready updates, recommendations, and action plans
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, clarify ownership, drive accountability, and move complex issues toward resolution

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The salary for this role will range from $134,600 - $230,800 annually based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and make the health system work better for everyone. We believe everyone-of every race, gender, sexuality, age, location and income-deserves the opportunity to live their healthiest life. Today, however, there are still far too many barriers to good health which are disproportionately experienced by people of color, historically marginalized groups and those with lower incomes. We are committed to mitigating our impact on the environment and enabling and delivering equitable care that addresses health disparities and improves health outcomes - an enterprise priority reflected in our mission.

UnitedHealth Group is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer under applicable law and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations.

UnitedHealth Group is a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment.

About the Role

The Assistant Vice President, HR Operations for Total Rewards will serve as the People team’s key operational and technology partner for global Total Rewards programs, including benefits, payroll, retirement, compensation, and leaves. Reporting to the Vice President, HR Technology, this role will improve the systems, data, integrations, and processes that support these programs.

Partnering closely with Total Rewards colleagues and other HR team members, this role will understand business needs, assess processes, identify requirements and dependencies, and translate these into practical system and operational solutions. The incumbent will also configure and test HR system functionality and oversee related work performed by third-party consultants, vendors, or technology partners. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who combines HR functional knowledge, systems experience, project management, analytical thinking, and a consultative, solution-oriented mindset.

Responsibilities

- Translate Total Rewards program requirements into operational workflows, functional specifications, system configuration, reports, controls, and integration designs, supported by clear documentation.

- Apply benefits and payroll expertise to assess how requirements affect employee records, eligibility, deductions, payroll results, vendor files, reporting, compliance, integrations, and employee experience.

- Analyze how evolving requirements affect employee records, eligibility, deductions, payroll results, vendor files, reporting, compliance, and the employee experience.

- Provide dedicated support for annual and recurring processes, including open enrollment, plan-year configuration, payroll changes, annual limits and rate updates, vendor and carrier implementations, integration changes, and other scheduled projects.

- Evaluate configuration and enhancement requests by clarifying the business problem, assessing impacts and dependencies, identifying risks, and recommending scalable solutions.

- Partner with external implementation and support resources while maintaining internal ownership of requirements, design decisions, configuration, testing, and solution quality.

- Review vendor recommendations critically to ensure proposed solutions address the underlying business need and are appropriate for the broader HR technology environment.

- Maintain documentation of system configurations, business rules, technical dependencies, decision rationales, and approved changes.

- Partner with internal and external technical resources and relevant HR subject matter experts to design, test, implement, monitor, and troubleshoot data feeds and system integrations.

- Develop a detailed understanding of inbound and outbound interfaces, including file layouts, field mappings, transformation rules, timing, dependencies, validation, error handling, reconciliation requirements, and downstream impacts.

- Conduct root-cause analysis when system, data, payroll, eligibility, or integration issues occur, and lead sustainable corrective actions. Ensure defects are documented, prioritized, resolved, retested, and formally closed.

- Promote clear ownership and governance for critical data elements, interfaces, operational controls, and issue resolution.

- Partner with HR stakeholders to understand business objectives, pain points, plan/policy requirements, service expectations, and operational risks.

- Identify opportunities to eliminate unnecessary steps, reduce manual intervention, strengthen controls, improve service delivery, and automate repeatable work.

- Support the development of a more resilient HR operating environment that reduces dependency on individual knowledge and third-party resources.

Qualifications

- 7+ or more years of progressive experience in payroll operations, benefits operations, HR business analysis or HR technology

- Experience implementing and managing Benefits, Payroll, Core HR, Reporting, and related modules within enterprise human capital management platforms such as Ceridian/Dayforce, including enhancements, upgrades, testing, release management, and production support

- Experience implementing and supporting HR data integrations, especially inbound and outbound carrier feeds

- Experience supporting annual and recurring HR processes, including open enrollment, plan-year configuration, payroll changes, rate updates, vendor and carrier implementations, and related integration changes

- Able to explain technical concepts to functional stakeholders and business requirements to technical stakeholders

- Sound judgment and discretion when working with sensitive payroll, benefits, and organizational data

- Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and experience working with large datasets to perform reconciliations, audit reports, and data analysis

- Project management, business analysis, HR, payroll, benefits, or HR technology certification is helpful but not required

- Experience using automation, workflow, or AI-assisted tools to improve documentation, analysis, controls, reporting, or service delivery, with appropriate human review and validation is preferred

Benefits

The base salary range for this role is $ 100,000 to $ 125,000.  iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO).

We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday.

For additional information on iCapital, please visit  https://www.icapitalnetwork.com/about-us   Twitter: @icapitalnetwork | LinkedIn:  https://www.linkedin.com/company/icapital-network-inc  | Awards Disclaimer:  https://www.icapitalnetwork.com/about-us/recognition/

iCapital is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

rows.title: Specialist Organizational Development
rows.note: Governance here means governance of the organisation design, and role architecture is read as job architecture.
rows.description:
Workplace Type:  Hybrid
Posting End Date:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our global headquarters in Denver, Colorado is a hub of innovation and collaboration. Here, multi-disciplinary teams chart strategy and provide technical, financial and operational leadership to support Newmont’s mines worldwide. Denver Hub’s professionals work closely with colleagues across all our regions, tackling projects that influence the entire business. The atmosphere is professional yet people-centered – we celebrate innovation and constantly seek better ways of working. Employees enjoy a modern workspace and the perks of a city famous for its outdoor lifestyle and vibrant economy.
Your Contribution

To support organizational health by delivering and improving Organizational Development systems, governance and assurance processes that strengthen design integrity and organizational effectiveness across Newmont.

As a part of our team, you will

- Maintain and continuously improve Organizational Development systems, governance processes, Ways of Working and supporting tools in alignment with enterprise standards.
- Support stewardship of the approved organizational design by maintaining its authorized representation and ensuring design decisions are appropriately documented.
- Support the development, application and continuous improvement of organization design standards, structural principles, role relationships, decision criteria and conformance requirements.
- Perform periodic, risk-based organizational design assurance reviews to assess material alignment with the approved design and evaluate whether surrounding governance and operational controls are working as intended.
- Analyze structural health indicators and enterprise patterns, including layers, spans, organizational capacity, cost and structural drift, to identify material risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Identify systemic patterns and distinguish isolated discrepancies from recurring breakdowns in processes, capabilities, workflows, governance or control design.
- Prepare governance reporting, structural health insights, assurance findings and management information to support decision-making, enterprise risk escalation and Organizational Development priorities.
- Support the governance and sustainment of the Role Profile Library, including intake, quality review, role profile reconciliation, role architecture alignment, version control and ongoing maintenance.
- Provide guidance to People Business Partners and other People stakeholders on the application of Organizational Development systems, standards, governance processes and design assurance requirements.
- Coordinate the implementation and sustainment of Organizational Development programs, tools and Ways of Working, including process documentation, guidance materials, capability support, adoption monitoring and continuous improvement.

Prerequisites for your success in this role

- Bachelor’s degree in organizational psychology, organizational development, business administration, social sciences, or related field.
- Advanced understanding of organizational design principles and organizational effectiveness concepts.
- Understanding of change management principles and frameworks, awareness of how to manage and support organizational change.
- Understanding of organizational governance, assurance and Health of Discipline concepts.
- Understanding of workforce planning, organizational analytics and role architecture.
- Knowledge of organizational design technologies, including Orgvue and related People platforms.
- Understanding of Role Profile Library governance, role architecture and organizational structure management practices.
- Advanced proficiency in Orgvue and organizational design data analysis.
- Advanced facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.
- Advanced written and verbal communications skills.
- Competent capability in workforce analytics, reporting and dashboard development.
- Competent capability in organizational assurance and governance processes.
- Competent understanding of role architecture, role profiling and organizational data structures.
- Competent capability in identifying trends, risks and improvement opportunities through data analysis.

Your work environment

This role operates within the Organization Development organization and partners closely with People Business Partners, Total Rewards, Talent Management, People Systems & Services, Workforce Planning and Business Planning as well as external consultants and advisors, industry associations and professional networks and technology platform providers.

Work Environment, Pay & Benefits:

This position is based in our Denver, CO corporate headquarters, with flexibility for hybrid work. The base salary range is 106,200- 141,600 (reflecting  market rates and your qualifications). The final base pay offer will be based on individual factors such as your experience, and skills – we do not ask for or use your prior pay in setting your compensation. You will also be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus based on company and personal performance. Newmont provides a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision insurance, health savings/reimbursement accounts, 401(k), pension, paid time off, and family leave.
Applying
When you apply, feel free to leave out age-related details like your birth date, graduation years or dates of attendance at educational institutions – it will not affect your application in any way.
Newmont and its affiliates are equal employment opportunity employers.  All qualified applicants for employment will be considered without regard to individual’s race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, religion, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. If you would like to request an accommodation in the application process due to a disability, please let your recruiter know. Newmont offers reasonable accommodations to candidates with disabilities.
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining. Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont Hear from our people: Life at Newmont

rows.title: Director Learning & Development
rows.note: Performance management and succession planning are asked only as an understanding of the talent ecosystem.
rows.description:
We take play seriously. We’re looking for curious adventurers ready to find their party, fueled by imagination and drive to build what’s never been built before. At Hasbro and Wizards of the Coast, you’ll collaborate with passionate teams to reimagine our iconic brands and create experiences that spark joy, connection, and community through the magic of play. This is your chance to shape legendary play that lasts a lifetime.

This is a unique opportunity to help build the future of learning at Hasbro, creating a development ecosystem that strengthens leadership, accelerates business-critical capabilities, and delivers learning experiences that are distinctly Hasbro.

The Director of Learning & Career Development will lead the design, development, and delivery of learning experiences that help our people grow and our business succeed. From onboarding and manager excellence to leadership development, workforce capability building, and differentiated talent programs, this leader will shape the learning experiences that support employees throughout their careers at Hasbro.

This is a highly visible role that requires strategic thinking, sound judgment, and hands-on execution. The ideal candidate is a builder who can create a roadmap, earn alignment, develop a team, roll up their sleeves, and bring programs to life. They are equally comfortable facilitating a leadership session, designing a new program, partnering with senior leaders, or leveraging technology and AI to scale impact across a global workforce.

A Day in the Life:

- Design & Execute Learning Strategy: Develop and evolve Hasbro's learning and career development roadmap, applying sound judgment to prioritize where we invest so learning supports business priorities, workforce needs, and employee growth.

- Partner Across the Business: Collaborate as a true team player with leaders, HR partners, and employees globally to assess capability needs, identify development opportunities, and create solutions that help teams and individuals perform at their best.

- Build & Deliver Learning Programs: Lead the design, development, facilitation, and delivery of high-impact learning experiences including onboarding, early career programs, manager excellence, leadership development, mentorship, coaching, and differentiated talent initiatives.

- Create Signature Hasbro Learning Experiences: Build distinctive, Hasbro-curated development experiences that strengthen culture, reinforce what great looks like at Hasbro, and help attract, engage, and retain top talent. Leverage internal expertise, executive involvement, business acumen, and the creativity of our brands to create learning experiences employees cannot get anywhere else.

- Build Critical Workforce Capabilities: Partner with business leaders to identify emerging skill needs and design scalable solutions that strengthen key capabilities such as AI, digital fluency, business acumen, leadership, and other enterprise priorities.

- Leverage Technology & AI to Scale Impact: Champion innovative learning technologies, AI-enabled tools, and emerging delivery methods that create engaging learning experiences, improve personalization, and extend the reach of a lean team. Continuously explore new approaches to learning and capability building.

- Activate Leaders as Teachers: Partner with executives and leaders to serve as teachers, mentors, coaches, and champions for learning across the organization.

- Integrate Learning with Talent, Culture & Inclusion: Collaborate across HR and business teams to embed learning into talent management, leadership expectations, performance practices, engagement, succession planning, and belonging initiatives.

- Measure & Communicate Impact: Apply critical thinking to data, insights, learner feedback, and business outcomes to evaluate effectiveness, demonstrate impact, and continuously improve programs.

- Build a High-Impact Learning Function: Lead, coach, and develop a small, agile team while creating scalable operating models, strong partnerships, and sustainable processes that maximize impact globally. Balance strategic leadership with hands-on ownership of program design, development, facilitation, and execution.

What You'll Bring

- 10+ years of progressive experience in Learning & Development coupled with Talent Management, Leadership Development, Organizational Development, or related HR disciplines.

- Demonstrated success building and scaling learning programs and capabilities in complex, matrixed, and global organizations.

- Experience managing a team of direct reports is required, with a demonstrated ability to coach, mentor, and support their career development through meaningful feedback, development planning, and opportunities for growth

- Experience balancing strategic leadership with hands-on program design, content creation, facilitation, implementation, and execution.

- Strong understanding of the broader talent ecosystem, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and organizational effectiveness.

- Proven ability to build trusted partnerships and influence leaders, HR partners, and stakeholders across functions, geographies, and cultures.

- Experience maximizing impact through lean teams, technology, innovative delivery models, and strategic vendor partnerships.

- Curiosity and enthusiasm for new technologies, evolving learning mediums, and innovative ways of building capability at scale.

- Strong data fluency, with the ability to define success measures, evaluate outcomes, and continuously improve programs.

- Experience engaging executives and senior leaders as active sponsors, teachers, coaches, and champions of development.

- Bonus: coaching certification; experience in manager excellence, leadership development, workforce capability building, talent acceleration, or early career programs.

The pay transparency range for this role is listed below. The hiring range will vary based on factors such as experience, skills, location and market conditions. Additionally, employees may be eligible for annual and long-term incentives as part of their overall compensation package.

Pay Range
$150,500 — $240,800 USD

Employees may be eligible for annual and long-term incentives as part of their overall compensation package, depending on role, location, and eligibility. Benefits and programs may include:

- Health & Wellness

- Time Off to Recharge

- Financial Well-being

- Life & Family Support

- Volunteer and Community Initiatives

- Learning & Development

- Exclusive Perks

rows.title: Sr. Manager, Global Compensation for Strategic Projects and Project Management
rows.description:
At Fluor, we are proud to design and build projects and careers. We are committed to fostering a welcoming and collaborative work environment that encourages big-picture thinking, brings out the best in our employees, and helps us develop innovative solutions that contribute to building a better world together. If this sounds like a culture you would like to work in, you’re invited to apply for this role.
Job Description

Summary
The Senior Compensation & Project Manager is a hybrid role responsible for strategic, enterprise-wide projects (designing, modeling, and scaling global compensation programs across all business segments globally), as well as coordinating the project management needs for the Global Compensation Team. This role requires a balance of analytical compensation expertise and rigorous project management. You will serve as the strategic engine driving the end-to-end execution of pay program redesigns, compensation cycle improvement initiatives and other key deliverables. The position combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, requiring expertise in compensation operations, analytics, and program management.

A core success component to this role is owning high-priority projects and programs end to end. You'll work closely with your Global Compensation and Executive Compensation teammates, as well as HRBPs, HRIS and other internal stakeholders, building expertise in how these programs work and what it takes to land them well.  You will identify dependencies early, proactively surface and mitigate risks, and keep complex, multi-stakeholder work moving toward clear outcomes. This is a high-level individual contributor role for someone who brings both rigor and judgment to every project they own.

Basic Job Requirements

Principal Job Duties & Responsibilities
- Leads and performs assigned enterprise-wide projects which span across business segments and geographies (such projects may include pay program redesign efforts, process improvement initiatives, support of compensation strategy development and analysis, etc.).
- Supports Global Compensation Team with project management techniques to drive improved execution across a portfolio of initiatives, ensuring that the organization is coordinated and on track to meet delivery of key solutions for the business.
- Administers the Project Status Tracker and develops reporting for senior leadership.
- Owns and delivers on various value-added projects as assigned.
- Develops dashboards which provide insights into talent management trends, pay competitiveness, labor market staffing dynamics, etc. to meet business needs and people-related objectives.
- Performs benchmarking and analysis to provide organizational compensation-related insights and recommendations for future actions.
- Participates in the Year-End Compensation Planning Cycle, both from an execution and process improvement standpoint.
- Works with the Global Compensation Team to drive towards best practices and consistent approaches and formats for supporting the various business segment customers.

Working Conditions
Indoor office workspace at the Irving, Texas headquarters.

Other Job Requirements

Preferred Qualifications

- 8 years of progressive experience in compensation, including program design and business partnering
- At least 3 years driving multi-stakeholder, cross-functional programs end to end, exercising strong project management skills (ideally at a scaling or global company)
- A track record of building from scratch: you've created processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure where none existed before, not just improved what was already in place
- Excellent written communication: you can produce an executive update, a stakeholder decision memo, and a practitioner playbook with equal fluency
- Strong foundation in global compensation programs, including multiple pay components (base pay and incentives)
- Proven ability to communicate complex compensation topics clearly and confidently to senior leadership, influencing decisions through data-driven insights
- Advanced Excel and analytical modeling skills to drive timely and high-quality delivery of insights
- Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect compensation strategy to Fluor’s business model and broader organizational goals
- Experience leading global compensation processes (e.g., annual cycles) across multiple stakeholder groups with a global mindset
- Advanced analytical skills, including compensation benchmarking, modeling, and insights generation
- Experience with SuccessFactors or similar HRIS/compensation platforms
- Track record of implementing compensation systems or tools and leading associated change management efforts, including process redesign and stakeholder enablement
- Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information with total discretion
- Self-starter with track record of proactively identifying and solving complex challenges

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified individuals will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other criteria protected by governing law.
Benefits Statement: Fluor is proud to offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to promote employee health, wellness, and financial security. Our offerings include medical, dental and vision plans, EAP, disability coverage, life insurance, AD&D, voluntary benefit plans, 401(k) with a company match, paid time off (personal, bereavement, sick, holidays) for salaried employees, paid sick leave per state requirement for craft employees, parental leave, and training and development courses.
Market Rate Statement: The market rate for the role is typically at the mid-point of the salary range; however, variations in final salary are determined by additional factors such as the candidate’s qualifications, relevant years of experience, geographic location, internal pay equity, and prevailing market conditions for the specific role.
Notice to Candidates: Background checks are carried out as part of any conditional offer made, including (but not limited to & role dependent) education, professional registration, employment, references, passport verifications and Global Watchlist screening.
To be Considered Candidates: Must be authorized to work in the country where the position is located.
Salary Range: $119,500.00 - $222,500.00

rows.title: Senior Workday Analyst, People Technology (Compensation)

rows.description:
CULTIVATE A BETTER WORLD

Food served fast does not have to be a typical fast-food experience. Chipotle has always done things differently, both in and out of our restaurants. We are changing the face of fast food, starting conversations, and directly supporting efforts to shift the future of farming and food. We hope you will join us as we continue to learn, evolve, and shape what comes next on our mission to make better food accessible to everyone.

THE OPPORTUNITY

As the Senior Workday Analyst, People Technology (Compensation), you will drive initiatives within the People Technology landscape focused on Core/Advanced Compensation, ensuring our systems effectively support our people-centric objectives. Your expertise will help optimize processes and enhance the overall employee experience, making a significant impact on our organizational effectiveness. In this role, you will lead complex system enhancements, collaborating with various stakeholders, to ensure the smooth execution of projects. By leading initiatives that align technology with our department strategy, you will ensure that People Technology remains agile and responsive to evolving needs. (Hybrid work schedule requiring 2 days per week onsite in either Newport Beach, CA or Columbus, OH headquarters).

WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Manage People Technology Workday projects focused on Core/Advanced Compensation improvements from inception to completion, ensuring timely and successful implementations; Experience with Total Value Matrix strongly preferred.
- Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders and product, to analyze business requirements and translate them into system solutions.
- Serve as a system administrator and Subject Matter Expert (SME) for People Tech systems, driving optimization of system configurations and ensuring data integrity across all IT systems.
- Provide technical leadership in analyzing system requirements, overseeing user acceptance testing (UAT), and ensuring successful execution of system upgrades and enhancements.
- Proactively identify opportunities to streamline business processes and recommend innovative solutions to improve functionality and user experience.
- Develop and maintain documentation, user guides, and training materials to support system changes and ensure effective knowledge transfer.
- Support production issues by providing case management, root cause analysis, and resolution of system incidents, while escalating complex issues to senior leadership as needed.
- Provide guidance to the team on best practices for system utilization and process improvements.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE TABLE
- Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Human Resources, or a related field (preferred).
- 5-8 years of HRIS experience, with a strong focus on Workday, including system administration and configuration expertise required.
- Subject matter expertise in HCM, Core and Advanced Compensation and experience in at least one of the following modules: Recruiting, Journeys, Learning or Paradox preferred; experience with Paradox is a plus.
- Proven ability to manage and lead multiple medium to large projects, from planning and execution through post-implementation support.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a demonstrated ability to troubleshoot issues and provide innovative solutions.
- Deep understanding of IT processes, including recruiting, benefits, compensation, and payroll, and how they integrate with people tech systems.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with stakeholders across departments.
- Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- A strategic mindset with the ability to think critically and translate technical concepts into user-friendly solutions.

PAY TRANSPARENCY

A reasonable estimate of the current base pay range for this position is $114,000.00–$160,500.00. You are also eligible for annual cash bonuses and equity awards based upon performance and other factors. Actual compensation offered may vary depending on skill level, experience, and/or education. Chipotle offers a competitive total rewards package, which includes medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401k, sick leave, vacation time, and much more. Visit https://jobs.chipotle.com/benefits for more details.
WHO WE ARE

Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. (NYSE: CMG) is cultivating a better world by serving responsibly sourced, classically cooked, real food with wholesome ingredients without artificial colors, flavors or preservatives. Chipotle has restaurants in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France and Germany and is the only restaurant company of its size that owns and operates all its restaurants in North America and Europe. With employees passionate about providing a great guest experience, Chipotle is a longtime leader and innovator in the food industry. Chipotle is committed to making its food more accessible to everyone while continuing to be a brand with a demonstrated purpose as it leads the way in digital, technology and sustainable business practices. For more information or to place an order online, visit WWW.CHIPOTLE.COM

Chipotle Mexican Grill is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity at all levels. As a people-first company rooted in values, our purpose extends beyond serving nutritious food using real ingredients. It means hiring world-class individuals and fostering a culture that champions diversity, ensures equity, and celebrates inclusion. rows.description:
Job Classification:
Corporate - Risk

Are you looking to grow your career within Operational Risk Management and deepen your understanding of financial services products under the Asset Management umbrella? Are you looking to diversify your skill set by expanding your analytical skill s with a growing organization? Our PGIM Operational Risk Management team is seeking a Manager   who will be responsible for collaborating closely with other control functions to promote operational risk awareness , and partner on key risks and initiatives .

Who are we?

PGIM is a top global fixed income asset manager w ith over $ 1 .47 tr illion in assets under management. Our parent company is Prudential Financial, Inc.

PGIM maintains a collegial and supportive work environment that promotes and rewards individual contributions while placing equal importance on results of the larger team. Associates within PGIM Operational Risk Management share their insights, skills, and diverse perspectives with a talented team working toward common goals. We place high priority on maintaining a work environment that develops, motivates, rewards, and retains employees.  We offer a total rewards package that includes competitive pay, performance-based incentives, long-term savings opportunities, and just as important , support for life beyond work.

Our Operational Risk Management team is a dynamic group that collaborates with all areas of PGIM ; in turn , creating a myriad of learning opportunities and a collaborative culture .   The role covers the PGIM Credit investment capability, which is comprised of Fixed Income and Private Credit groups.
The team serves as an internal business pa rtner in establish ing and maintain ing an effective system of internal control s.

Responsibilities

- Conduct detailed risk assessments/control reviews for existing processes, new products , and initiatives by e nsuring key operational risks and controls are properly identified , assessed and documente d .

- Review and analyze errors/incidents and other risk events including perform ing root cause analysis and recommend corrective measures (including assisting with implementation ).

- Report to Senior Management on key operational risks, significant risk events, status of outstanding issues , and other topics

- Assist in the collection and reporting of key risk indicators (KRIs), top risks, and other risk related metrics and reporting.

- Promote Prudential’s Operational Risk Management framework policies and procedures across the PGIM Credit business es

- Monitor, analyze and communicate emerging risks and external events

- Collaborate closely with Portfolio Managers in Fixed Income and Private Credit , along with th e support functions across the business to reinforce operational risk ownership and accountably .

- Act as an Internal Audit liaison, including planning and coordination for internal audits, as well as assist ing in the development, monitoring and closure of audit related action plans

- S upport Sarbanes-Oxley and SOC1 annual reviews including assisting with scop e determi nation, collaborating w ith inte rnal and extern al au dit an d issues management

- Collaborate closely with other control functions including Compliance, Legal and Internal Audit on risk/control related items

- Assist with the management , policy requirements and ongoing monitoring over Models, Artificial Intelligence (AI ) and End User Computing Solutions (EUCS)

- Support business transformation activities across PGIM Credit while assessing and mitigating risk associated with business and technology changes .

Qualifications

- Extensive business knowledge in the fixed income industry encompassing public fixed income and private credit , specifically trade lifecycle activities and operational support

Compliance Director The Opportunity:
Booz Allen is looking for an experienced compliance leader to help shape how our compliance capability supports a business evolving across technology, government missions, partnerships, acquisitions, and new ways of delivering for customers.

As Director, Compliance, you will oversee an experienced team responsible for a portfolio of compliance and integrity programs and shape how Legal, Ethics & Compliance (LEC) identifies, assesses, and responds to compliance risk. You will advise the Chief Ethics & Compliance Officer (CECO) and other leaders on complex matters, changing risks, and where action is needed.

You will also connect specialized compliance programs across LEC that sit with different leaders, creating a shared view of compliance risk and program effectiveness while preserving each program leader’s accountability and expertise. You will bring those perspectives together, challenge whether risks and issues are being addressed appropriately, and surface matters that require action across programs or leadership attention.

This role offers the opportunity to lead complex compliance work, influence decisions across the business, advise executives, and evolve our approach to compliance. Due to the nature of work performed within this facility, U.S. citizenship is required.

What You'll Do:
- Set priorities for the Compliance capability within LEC and advance how we identify, manage, and assess compliance risk.
- Oversee a portfolio of compliance programs, including anti-corruption, third-party integrity, government contractor compliance, conflicts of interest, competition, lobbying, and related areas, with experienced program leaders providing subject-matter leadership for their programs.
- Guide and challenge compliance program leaders on complex matters, changing risks, program priorities, and issues requiring action or escalation.
- Lead the compliance risk assessment, using input from across Compliance, changes in the business and regulatory environment, investigations, audits, monitoring, and other evidence to identify changing exposure, gaps, and priorities.
- Strengthen how compliance programs are evaluated and improved, using evidence and outcomes to identify root causes, address gaps, and improve program effectiveness.
- Advise on compliance risk as the business changes, including new offerings, partnerships, acquisitions, and regulatory developments, working with Legal, business, and functional leaders to address risks early.
- Maintain a connected view across Compliance, identifying shared risks and issues, challenging whether they are being appropriately addressed, and surfacing matters requiring broader action or CECO attention.
- Advise the CECO and executive leadership and support Audit Committee engagement on compliance risk, program effectiveness, open issues and remediation, emerging risks, and priorities requiring leadership attention.

Join us. The world can't wait.

You Have:
- 10+ years of experience as an attorney advising on corporate, regulatory, government contractor, or compliance matters
- Experience leading multiple compliance programs and capabilities, experienced professionals, or cross-functional initiatives
- Experience advising executives on legal, regulatory, compliance, or integrity matters and their potential business impacts
- Experience leading compliance risk assessments, governance, monitoring, issue management, remediation, controls, or program effectiveness
- Experience with compliance areas such as anti-corruption, third-party integrity, government contracting, transactions, conflicts, competition, lobbying, or risks
- JD degree
- Active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar

Nice If You Have:
- Experience in a broad compliance leadership or a similar role in a regulated or complex organization
- Experience in a publicly traded company, U.S. government contractor, or similarly regulated organization
- Experience advising a CECO, General Counsel, executive leadership team, or Board or Audit Committee
- Experience working in a distributed compliance model where programs have different accountable leaders
- Experience influencing decisions and establishing accountability across organizational boundaries, including with teams that do not report directly to you
- Knowledge of DOJ expectations, regulatory and enforcement developments, and recognized practices for effective corporate compliance programs
- Ability to combine legal and compliance judgment, credible challenge, and practical business judgment
- Ability to synthesize legal, regulatory, business, and program information into clear risk assessments, priorities, recommendations, and decisions

Compensation
At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $185,700.00 to $345,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.
Identity Statement
As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

Candidate AI Usage Policy
AI is a part of our daily work at Booz Allen, and we are committed to the responsible and ethical use of AI tools. However, we want to ensure a fair candidate process based on your own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) or other tools to assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is prohibited unless permission is explicitly provided .

Work Model
Our people-first culture prioritizes the benefits of collaboration. To support engagement and effective communication, employees working virtually are generally expected to have their cameras on during meetings.
- Remote : If this position is listed as remote, there may still be occasions when you are required to work in person at a Booz Allen or customer facility.

As AI agents and automation spread across Finance, our governance lead will build the intake, risk triage, and approval flow that lets the right tools move quickly and keeps the wrong ones away from financial data. rows.title: Business Operations, MBA Intern

rows.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The business operations team at Base is a lean group of generalists who take high-stakes, not-very-defined problems, give them structure, and drive them to completion. As our MBA intern, you'll get a real piece of that work for the summer, not a side project. You'll pick up a defined slice of whatever the team is running right now (today that's the integration of a recent acquisition; it could also be a commercial partnership or a market entry) and drive it to a decision.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Cover one part of the business for the summer: know its plan, its unit costs, and its tradeoffs better than anyone outside the team.

 - Own a discrete project inside it end to end — the forecast it runs on, a market or product entry, a workstream in an acquisition integration, or the scoreboard it's missing — and leave behind something that still runs without you.

 - Structure the problem yourself; define the goal, name the owners, write the memo that forces the tradeoff.

 - Build the analysis yourself — the model, the scoreboard, the one-pager — and defend the assumptions to the people who have to hit them.

 - Get into the data yourself; our warehouse, our install and market data, our AI tooling, rather than waiting on someone to pull it for you.

 - Work across functions without formal authority; rally owners in engineering, market operations, manufacturing, accounting, and customer operations.

 - Spend time where the money actually gets spent: ride along on an install, sit with market operations, walk the manufacturing floor.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Currently pursuing an MBA, returning for your second year in the fall.

 - 2–5 years of pre-MBA experience.

 - Comfort in data; SQL already, or a real willingness to be writing it in week one.

 - Comfort operating without a map; you create structure where none exists.

 - Low ego, high ownership. We are people others want to work with, and there is no “that's not my job”.

 - Fluency working alongside AI; you use it to multiply your output and know when to check its work.




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Base business operations team is responsible for some of the company's highest-leverage outcomes: financing our growth, commercial partnerships, acquisitions and integrations, new market and product entries, and the programs that span too many teams to have a natural owner. It is a set of small teams of generalists who work directly with Base's founders, pick up the problem that matters most, build the structure and analysis it needs, and hand back something that runs itself.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.
